dataset: Red-flag registry — the structured safety layer for diagnostic entities
policy: One record per (entity, trigger). This registry is the CANONICAL home of red flags going forward; red_flags_zh/_en on cards are PRESENTATION, derived into the bundle at build time (scripts/build-data.js merges registry triggers into the card's arrays — source files are never rewritten).

Legacy inline red_flags_zh/_en already authored on cards (e.g. the 25 gyn records, 2026-08) stay authored in place until migrated batch by batch; the build-time merge deduplicates, so a migrated trigger never renders twice.

Every record MUST carry at least one evidence entry with an https source_url from the docs/COND_INGESTION_SPEC.md whitelist. A red flag without a source does not get written — 查不到就是答案, it stays a gap in the fill queue, never an invented trigger (AI_CONSTITUTION).

entity_id may be cond.* or tdis.* (shared-safety rule, v2 spec §28: never duplicate the same warning prose across namespaces by hand — give the second entity its own record only when the trigger genuinely differs).

Patient-level safety flags (pregnancy, anticoagulants, pacemaker…) are a DIFFERENT layer: data/config/safety_flag_vocabulary.json + case safetyFlags. This registry is per-diagnosis referral triggers, not per-patient status.

Why this exists as a sidecar instead of richer card fields: future Case/Visit safety screening needs stable per-flag identity (screened / present / absent per visit) and a tier machine-readable for decision support. Strings on cards cannot carry identity — renaming a string orphans every clinical record that referenced it. Structured now avoids that migration (Ting, 2026-08-08).
